key_insight: LLM uncertainty helped identify stenosis extraction errors but did not improve detection of disagreement between CCTA and subsequent invasive angiography.
clinical_relevance: Uncertainty may support quality checks on LLM-derived clinical datasets, but it should not be treated as a signal of underlying clinical discordance.
method: Extracted vessel-level coronary stenosis severity from reports in a 1,045-patient CCTA cohort.
Compared extractions with expert CCTA annotations and compared CCTA findings with subsequent invasive coronary angiography.
Evaluated Stenosis Margin uncertainty using adjusted logistic regression and AUC.
evidence_signal: Expert annotations covered 253 patients and invasive angiography 729; uncertainty improved extraction-error discrimination (reported ΔAUC +0.06) but not clinical-discordance discrimination, and 38 of 42 discordant vessels were extracted correctly.
watch_item: Stenosis Margin was selected from ten candidate measures; its reliability in other cohorts and reporting settings needs validation.
paper_title: Distinguishing Extraction Failures and Clinical Discordance with LLM Uncertainty on Radiology Reports
